entities.summary:
Brothers of Italy (Fratelli d'Italia, FdI), founded in 2012 by Giorgia Meloni from the post-fascist National Alliance and its MSI predecessor, became the largest Italian party and formed Italy's most right-wing government since World War II after the September 2022 elections. Meloni became Italy's first female prime minister and the first post-fascist leader of a G7 country — her party still features the tricolor flame of the MSI (founded by Mussolini loyalists in 1946) as its official symbol.

Fratelli d'Italia traces its lineage directly from the Italian Social Movement (MSI, 1946-1994) — founded by Mussolini loyalists and using the fascist tricolor flame symbol. The post-war Italian democratic system systematically excluded MSI from government coalitions (the arco costituzionale). Gianfranco Fini's 1994 transformation of MSI into National Alliance, and his embrace of democratic norms, broke the exclusion partially. Meloni's 2012 founding of FdI after the National Alliance merged with Berlusconi's Forza Italia maintained the tricolor flame continuity.

Meloni's 2022 victory came from a rightward shift of Italian voters exhausted by coalition instability — Italy had 69 governments in 76 years since 1946. Her government combined conservative social policy (opposition to LGBTQ+ rights, immigration restriction) with Atlanticist foreign policy (supporting Ukraine against Russia) and a pragmatic relationship with EU institutions — confounding predictions of a Eurosceptic populist governance. The FdI coalition's durability tested whether Italy's political system had finally achieved governmental stability.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Brothers of Italy's 2022 victory — installing the first post-fascist leader of a G7 country, from a party still using Mussolini-era symbols — represents the furthest normalization of far-right politics in Western European governance since the end of World War II.
